project.title: It's All Our Blood
project.maker: Pentagram / Harry Pearce for the University of Maryland Art Gallery
project.format: Commemorative exhibition poster paired with a process film

why: A strong poster reference for building the entire argument around one physical image-making experiment: the page shows how a single red cloud photograph, strict white space, and restrained timing annotations can carry memorial weight without decorative clutter.

compositions.title: Isolated blood-cloud focal image
compositions.study: The core image is a photograph of a drop of blood hitting water, held alone so the resulting red cloud reads like an atomic blast rather than a collage of symbols.
compositions.reuse: Use one dominant metaphor image when a poster needs immediate symbolic force and should not dilute the concept with secondary illustrations.

compositions.title: High-contrast white memorial field
compositions.study: The project sets the image on a white background, letting the red cloud do nearly all of the emotional work while the surrounding negative space keeps the poster solemn and legible.
compositions.reuse: Use a large unprinted field when the subject matter benefits from silence, pause, or gallery-like framing.

compositions.title: Time-and-place annotation strip
compositions.study: Grey and black type marks the locations and times of the bombings, turning factual metadata into part of the composition instead of a detached caption block.
compositions.reuse: Fold documentary details into the poster grid when context should sharpen the concept without competing with the hero image.

assets.notes: The final poster image came from repeated physical tests with blood, water temperature, and drop height, then a last-frame photograph by Richard Foster.
assets.reuse: Prototype the central image materially when the poster concept depends on texture, unpredictability, or physical truth.

assets.notes: The supporting typography stays grey and black, functioning as factual annotation rather than expressive decoration.
assets.reuse: Keep contextual type subdued when the image carries the emotional peak.

assets.role: supporting evidence of the image-making method
assets.notes: A behind-the-scenes film extends the poster by documenting the path from blood draw to photography studio to printmaking.
assets.reuse: Add process documentation when the making method is part of the poster's meaning and can deepen trust in the concept.

motion.title: Poster-making documentary extension
motion.notes: The accompanying film reframes the poster as a deliberate physical experiment instead of a digitally composited effect.
motion.fallback: If no motion companion exists, preserve the same making-story through still process frames or a concise caption.

implementation.format: Concept-led photographic poster with restrained annotation and a supporting process film
implementation.notes: The Pentagram page provides enough source evidence to keep this as an accepted poster reference: concept statement, physical image-making method, typographic treatment, and the existence of a process-film companion are all explicit.

capture.attribution: Pentagram; Harry Pearce; photography by Richard Foster; client University of Maryland Art Gallery
